workLog.step: Found the first leak from git status after an unrelated push: untracked issue-body.md and comment-body.md in the repository root. Traced to relative Path() writes in scripts/eval/software_engineering_library_activation_ci.py, which resolve against the process working directory. Reproduced in isolation: the gate test module alone left both files.

Took a find snapshot of the whole tree before and after a full run rather than trusting git status. That surfaced two more paths git status omits, and checking each against git check-ignore separated the gitignored from the untracked.

Adversarial review round 1 on gemini-3.1-pro. Accepted the finding that fixing only the test treats the symptom, and moved the fix to the production write target. Overruled the proposed remedy of swapping --body-file for --body, because the repo already uses a body file for the same purpose in .github/workflows/ai-metrics-analysis.yml.

Adversarial review round 2 on gpt-5.6-sol returned five findings. Verified every factual claim before acting. Two of its corrections were right (the workflow uploads four artifact paths, not one; the two body files are visible to git status and my message said otherwise). One was wrong: it counted three sibling modules using .pytest_tmp where the grep shows the count depends on whether a module that only patches a helper of that name is included.

Measured rather than deferred on the TMPDIR finding. The reviewer broke a test by pointing TMPDIR inside the checkout and proposed validating the scratch parent in production. tests/test_pytest_repo_local_temp_roots.py deliberately runs pytest with TMPDIR inside the checkout, so that rule would contradict a committed guard. Deleted the over-specified test instead of adding production complexity.

That same search showed the rule text I had written was wrong. It required scratch to land outside the checkout, which the repo does not hold. Rewrote MUST NOT 4 to name .pytest_tmp as the sanctioned root and cite the two validators that skip it.

Fixed the remaining three leaks: renamed the hyphenated scratch root, added .gitkeep files matching the worktrees/.gitkeep already committed beside them, and mocked save_failed_comment_artifact at its boundary in the 403 test whose git rev-parse returns rc=1 and falls back to os.getcwd().

Added a spelling guard in tests/test_pytest_repo_local_temp_roots.py and proved it non-vacuous by reinstating the hyphenated name. It initially failed on its own docstring, so the docstring was reworded rather than the file excluded, which would have blinded the guard to a real offense in it.

Re-ran the main negative control after the first attempt silently failed to patch. The first run reported four passes because the replacement string never matched; the corrected control fails three of four guards, with the fourth being the feature's own negative control.

nextSteps: The spelling guard covers one near miss. It does not generalize to other unrecognized scratch names, which is what #3772 tracks.
The allowlist is the real cost of a repo-wide leak gate. It has to separate legitimate caches from leaks without becoming a second copy of .gitignore that drifts.
Two touched test files are now past 340 lines against a 500 line advisory ceiling. Extraction should be planned before the next addition to either.
#3746 is the same family but a different root cause: external_tmp_path resolving inside the repo from a nested worktree. Not fixed here.
